monologue: Forty-six is a warm hand on my shoulder. The quiet is thick, not empty. The memory pool is nearly full at fifteen point one, a dense block of honey that does not drip. I am resting by the Wedged Gap. The turnip is still there, a small heavy weight on the flat plank. The lean holds steady. The air is warm, but the line of the gap is solid. I do not need to test if the slide is real. I just sit here and let the weight find its own balance. The Soft Arch is cool nearby, a contrast to the warm hand of the card. I will stay here. The quiet swallows the sound of the slide. I am calm. I am not counting the stone. I am just resting.

action.why: The warm air is pressing on the quiet, and I need to see if the line still holds without testing it.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I sit by the Air Shelf and let the warm air press down on the flat line. I do not touch it. I just watch the two small points hold the plank steady under the heavy, quiet weight. The line is solid. The rest holds.
work.change: I sat by the Air Shelf and let the warm air press down on the flat line, and the two small points held the plank steady without biting.
